docs.title: 1. Upload genomic data and set configurations
docs.text:
• From the Home page, choose “Carrier Screening - Family. Click "Continue".
  • Input sample name, upload genomic data in compressed VCF format (.vcf.gz), and upload PED file illustrating the parents' relationship.
  • Upload customized screening panel (.txt/.tsv) or select one or more preset screening lists.
  • Select reference genome version.
  • Set the parameters for filtering variants (global minor allele frequency, predicted scores, clinical pathogenicity).
  • Enter any of the PGS Catalog Identifiers if needed.
  • Select to run PGx profiling or not.
  • Click "Submit" to proceed.

docs.title: 2. View Results
docs.text: The submitted job and job status are presented in "Analysis Jobs" on the homepage. \ Once the job is completed, click the job name to view all results. \ Results are organized into 6 sections: - Family Information: This section summarizes the family relationships from PED file. - Variant Summary: This section summarizes clinical P/LP variants (both ClinVar or ACMG P/LP). - Disease Carrier Status: This section presents the recessive disease that would be potentially transmitted to the offspring. These diseases are caused by both ClinVar and ACMG P/LP variants. - Pharmacogenomics: This section provides a report for each family member summarizing all identified pharmacogenomics diplotypes in the newborns via PharmCat. Detailed explanations and recommendations are illustrated in the structured report. - Polygenic Risk Scores: This section provides polygenic scores of each family member and reference population regarding the required PGS model. The similarity scores are also provided for genetic clustering. Information is also summarized into a strctured report. - Variant Details: This section presents all details for the filtered variants.

docs.title: 3. Choose pathogenic variants and potential diseases to be included in the final PDF report.
docs.text:
FamilyRisk provides a template for clinical reporting, where users can further customize the report by selecting specific results and adding professional advice, suggestions, and comments. 1) In "Screen-positive Results", "Disease Carrier Status", and "Variant Details" sections, switch the button under "Include" to include or exclude the specific variant to be presented in the final report.

2) Click "Report Generation" to generate the report.

3) Add additional analytical texts, recommendations, and references via the portal. 4) Set the report language. Options: English, Turkish, Spanish, Korean, Chinese, Japanese. 5) Click "Continue" to view the final digital report.

6) Download, print, or re-edit the report following the previous steps.

docs.title: 4. Export Data
docs.text:
• Results in each section could be downloaded separately.
  • All results could be wrapped up and downloaded as a zipped file by clicking the download button in the bottom-right corner.

docs.title: Database
docs.text: The FamilyRisk database is a unified resource for carrier and newborn screening. It could be found under "Database" on the homepage.

docs.title: Overview
docs.text: The database information is summarized in the "Overview". It integrates 3,112 curated gene–disease associations derived from seven leading NBSeq projects and two ACMG recommendations, collectively covering 15 disease ontologies.

docs.title: Projects
docs.text: Each of the projects collected in this database could be reviewed in the "Projects". By clicking the project name/logo, project information, filtering criteria for pathogenic variants, clinical returned results, and quick links to the official website and relevant publications can be referred to. More importantly, the detailed screening list of each project is presented as well.

docs.title: Screening Results
docs.text: The clinical returned results of five newborn sequencing projects are summarized in the "Screening Results". Notably, only BabySeq and EarlyCheck disclosed the screen-positive carrier status.

docs.title: Generator
docs.text: FamilyRisk Database offers the Screening List Generator, enabling users to customize gene-disease associations outside the collections. This tool displays all curated associations collected in the database, with the corresponding disease inheritance modes, OMIM identifiers, disease ontologies, originating projects, and GenCC classifications and submitters. Users could select subgroups of the screening lists and disease inheritance modes via “Advanced Filters”. Additional gene-disease associations could be manually added into the full list via the “Quick Add Custom Entry” function by specifying the gene symbol, disease name, and other relevant details. All customized entries will be added to the end of the main table, while the wrong ones could be easily cleared. Eventually, the full list or selected associations could be downloaded locally and applied to the downstream genomic data analysis in the main portal.

docs.title: A Free-Access, Integrated Web Server for Early-Life Disease Screening and Clinical Reporting
docs.text: 📍 Access FamilyRisk: https://www.phenomeportal.org/familyrisk

docs.title: 1️⃣ Comprehensive Screening Database
docs.text:
FamilyRisk integrates curated knowledge on screening strategies, gene–disease associations, and clinical outcomes to support screening study design and clinical decision-making.

The database aggregates evidence from seven established newborn sequencing initiatives (BabySeq, BabyScreen+, BabyDetect, GUARDIAN, EarlyCheck, Genomics 101, NBScreening), ACMG Secondary Findings, and ACMG Expanded Carrier Screening.

docs.title: 2️⃣ Flexible Panel Customization
docs.text:
The Screening List Generator embedded in the database allows users to:

  • Select preset screening lists
  • Add or remove gene–disease associations
  • Create customized panels tailored to specific clinical or research needs

This feature supports adaptable implementation across diverse screening scenarios.

docs.title: 3️⃣ Versatile Genomic Analysis
docs.text: FamilyRisk streamlines genomic analysis at the individual, family, and population level. It supports interpretation of small variants (SNVs/indels), copy number variants, and structural variants. Compatible with both GRCh37 and GRCh38 reference genomes.

docs.title: 4️⃣ Segregation Analysis
docs.text: FamilyRisk provides integrated segregation analysis to evaluate inheritance patterns and assess transmission of pathogenic variants within families.

docs.title: 5️⃣ Polygenic Risk Evaluation & Pharmacogenomics Profiling
docs.text: FamilyRisk enables polygenic score (PGS) evaluation for complex diseases and common traits. It also compares individual's PGS against the reference populations to estimate genetic susceptibility. It phases Pharmacogenomic (PGx) diplotype to provide Evidence-based therapeutic recommendations.

docs.title: 6️⃣ Flexible Clinical Reporting
docs.text:
FamilyRisk separates results into structured sub-panels for clarity and usability.

Users can:

  • Select specific variants or diseases
  • Generate customizable clinical PDF reports
  • Add professional comments, clinical interpretations, and recommendations

This facilitates translation from genomic data to actionable clinical documentation.

docs.title: 📘 Tutorials
docs.text:
• The step-by-step video tutorial could be found:
  • [Video]

Each function of FamilyRisk is documented with step-by-step Markdown guides:

Function Description Tutorial Database Integrated knowledge of carrier and newborn screening projects, gene panels, and clinical outcomes. View Tutorial Newborn Screening-Individual Individual-level newborn screening. Identify potential monogenic rare diseases and disease carrier status. View Tutorial Newborn Screening-Family Family-level newborn screening. Identify potential monogenic rare diseases and disease carrier status in the newborns. Segregation analysis to visualize variant inheritance patterns. View Tutorial Newborn Screening-Population Cohort-level newborn screening. Identify regional prevalent monogenic rare diseases and disease carrier status. Calculate cohort-level allele frequency. View Tutorial Newborn Screening-CNV/SV Annotate individual-level copy number variants and structural variants in the newborn. View Tutorial Carrier Screening-Individual Individual-level carrier screening. Identify potential recessive diseases that might inherit by the offspring. View Tutorial Carrier Screening-Family Couple-level carrier screening. Identify potential recessive diseases that might inherit by the offspring. View Tutorial

docs.title: 🔹 Individual-level Newborn Screening for Copy Number Variants and Structural Variants
1. Upload genomic data and set configurations
docs.text:
• From the Home page, choose “Newborn Screening - CNV / Structural Variant Analysis. Click "Continue".
  • Input sample name, upload genomic data in compressed VCF format (.vcf.gz)
  • Upload additional SNVs/INDELs compressed VCF format files (.vcf.gz) to detect the compound heterozygous deletions in CNV/SV.
  • Upload customized screening panel (.txt/.tsv) or select one or more preset screening lists.
  • Select reference genome version.
  • Select variant type. Options: CNV, SV.
  • Click "Submit" to proceed.
